mainTopic: Wrong thoughts during טבילה and הולכה of a חטאת's blood: when they disqualify, according to the רבנן and רבי שמעון, and whether a זר may carry the blood.
overview: Two ברייתות seemed to argue about whether a wrong thought during dipping the finger in the blood (טבילה) can make a חטאת פיגול. The גמרא rejects the idea that one of them follows רבי שמעון. Instead it says both follow the רבנן: with inner חטאות dipping is a real step, because the Torah writes 'וטבל', but with outer חטאות it is not. The גמרא explains that the Torah wrote 'ולקח' for outer חטאות, which teaches two things at once. Next, ריש לקיש says רבי שמעון agrees that a wrong thought while carrying the blood of inner חטאות disqualifies, because that carrying can never be skipped. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explains that this makes them פסול, not פיגול, through a קל וחומר. The גמרא then finds a source for a wrong thought about place, either from שלא לשמה or from a הקש in the פסוק. רבא shows, through a chain of 'if he holds this' cases, how the carrying that truly counts can shrink to a doorway, a hand-stretch, or nothing at all. Finally אביי asks whether a זר may carry the blood, and רב חסדא says yes, citing a פסוק. רב ששת begins a challenge from a ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's rule blocks the suggested answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge. רבי שמעון holds that any offering not placed on the outer altar like שלמים has no פיגול at all, so he cannot be the source of a ברייתא that discusses פיגול with inner offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: [But רבי שמעון said that] any offering that is not placed on the outer altar the way a peace offering is cannot become פיגול!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of a challenge. The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's rule to knock down the suggestion that one of the two ברייתות follows him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, פיגול only applies to offerings whose blood goes on the מזבח החיצון, like שלמים. Inner חטאות do not fit that model, so for him they have no פיגול at all. That makes it impossible to say a ברייתא about פיגול during טבילה reflects his view.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering made invalid because the כהן intended to eat it or offer it after its proper time
The outer altar in the courtyard
Peace offerings, the standard model for the laws of פיגול

phrases.english: Any offering that is not on the outer altar
like a peace offering is not subject to piggul!

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ עַל מִזְבֵּחַ הַחִיצוֹן כִּשְׁלָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge that began before this section, against the idea that one ברייתא follows רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the contradiction between the two ברייתות comes from רבי שמעון disagreeing with the רבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון holds that offerings not placed on the outer altar have no פיגול at all, so he would not discuss פיגול during טבילה of inner חטאות.

steps.title: Both follow the Rabbis: outer versus inner sin offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer. Both ברייתות follow the רבנן. The one that says טבילה cannot create פיגול speaks of חטאות החיצוניות, and the one that says it can speaks of חטאות הפנימיות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, both ברייתות follow the רבנן, and there is no contradiction. One speaks about outer sin offerings, and the other speaks about inner sin offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the רבי שמעון idea. It settles the contradiction by saying the two ברייתות are talking about different kinds of חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For inner חטאות the Torah writes 'וטבל', so dipping is a real part of the service and wrong intent during it can create פיגול. For outer חטאות dipping is not a main part of the service, so wrong intent during it does nothing. The disagreement is now about two different cases, not two different opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one, meaning both sources
Sin offerings whose blood is placed on the outer altar
Sin offerings whose blood is brought inside, toward the inner altar or the פרוכת
It is not difficult; the contradiction is resolved

steps.whatToRemember: Both ברייתות follow the רבנן. With inner חטאות, טבילה can create פיגול. With outer חטאות, it cannot.

phrases.english: Rather, both this and that are the Rabbis
and it is not difficult
here, with external sin offerings
there, with inner sin offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא וְהָא רַבָּנַן, וְלָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected רבי שמעון answer with a new way to resolve the contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each ברייתא is about a different kind of offering.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות are two opinions, רבי שמעון and the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are the רבנן. One is about outer חטאות and the other is about inner חטאות.

steps.title: Isn't the rule for outer sin offerings obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a ברייתא would need to teach that טבילה for outer חטאות cannot create פיגול. The word 'וטבל' is not even written about them.
steps.simpleTranslation: About outer sin offerings, isn't it obvious? 'And he shall dip' is not written about them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If dipping is clearly not a main step for outer חטאות, why would the ברייתא bother to say so?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא does not usually teach something obvious. Since the Torah only writes 'וטבל' for inner חטאות, it seems clear that dipping does not count for outer ones. So the ברייתא's statement looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; why would it need to be taught?
'And he shall dip', the Torah's word for dipping the finger in the blood

phrases.english: External sin offerings — it's obvious!
"And he shall dip" is not written regarding them!

steps.triggerLanguage: חַטָּאוֹת הַחִיצוֹנוֹת – פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the half of Step 2's answer that is about outer חטאות.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's need to teach that טבילה for outer חטאות cannot create פיגול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah never writes 'וטבל' for outer חטאות, so there is no reason anyone would think dipping counts for them.

steps.title: It was needed: 'And he shall take' might count like dipping
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the teaching was needed. For outer חטאות the Torah writes 'ולקח'. If a monkey puts blood on the כהן's hand, he must take blood again himself. So one might think taking is just like dipping.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought that since 'and he shall take' is written, and if a monkey comes and puts blood on the כהן's hand he must take blood again, it is as if 'and he shall dip' were written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא's teaching is not obvious. It lays out the mistaken idea someone might have had, and the next step finishes the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Outer חטאות do have 'ולקח', taking blood with the finger. Because blood that lands on the hand by itself, like from a monkey, does not count, taking seems to be a required act, much like dipping. That is why the ברייתא had to say it still cannot create פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary to teach
It might have entered your mind to say, introducing a mistaken first idea
'And he shall take', the word used for outer חטאות
Monkey

steps.confusionAlert: This is only the mistaken first idea (הוה אמינא). The ברייתא teaches that we do NOT treat 'ולקח' like 'וטבל' when it comes to פיגול.

phrases.english: It was necessary; it might enter your mind to say
since it is written "and he shall take"
and if a monkey comes
and places [the blood] on his hand
he must take [blood] another time
it is as if "and he shall dip" were written;

steps.triggerLanguage: אִצְטְרִיךְ; סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 3's 'פשיטא' challenge by showing the teaching was not obvious.
steps.terutzResolutionType: איצטריך: shows the teaching was needed by giving a reasonable mistaken idea.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since 'ולקח' requires the כהן himself to take the blood, and a monkey's help does not count, taking might be treated like 'וטבל', so it could create פיגול.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא teaches that for outer חטאות, טבילה still cannot create פיגול. Step 5 gives the full reason: the Torah wrote ולקח and not וטבל.

steps.title: Why the Torah wrote 'take' and not 'dip'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer. The ברייתא teaches that dipping for outer חטאות is not a real עבודה. The Torah chose the word ולקח because it teaches two things at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the ברייתא teaches us: this is why 'and he shall dip' is not written. The word 'take' means this and also means that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the answer from Step 4. It explains why the ברייתא needed to say that dipping for outer חטאות cannot cause פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ולקח teaches that the כהן must take the blood himself, which is the monkey case. Because the Torah did not write וטבל, we also learn that dipping is not a real עבודה for outer חטאות. So a wrong thought during dipping cannot create פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches us (the new point being made)
And he shall dip (the finger in the blood)
It means this and it means that: one word teaching two things

steps.whatToRemember: For outer חטאות, the Torah wrote ולקח, not וטבל. So the כהן must take the blood himself, but dipping is not an עבודה that can create פיגול.

phrases.english: It teaches us:
for this reason 'and he shall dip' is not written,
so that it means this and it means that.
phrases.notes: The word ולקח does two jobs: the כהן must take the blood himself, and dipping is not a real עבודה here.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in Step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the ברייתא's teaching was needed to stop a mistaken assumption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since ולקח requires the כהן to actively take the blood, one might think taking counts like dipping and can create פיגול
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah avoided the word וטבל, so dipping for outer חטאות is not an עבודה that creates פיגול

steps.title: רבי שמעון agrees about carrying the blood of inner חטאות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: רבי שמעון says a wrong thought while carrying the blood does not disqualify. ריש לקיש says רבי שמעון agrees that for inner חטאות it does disqualify, because that carrying can never be skipped.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says רבי שמעון holds the offering valid if the wrong thought was while carrying the blood. ריש לקיש said: רבי שמעון agrees that for inner חטאות, a wrong thought while carrying disqualifies, since that carrying is a service that can never be skipped.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic: רבי שמעון's opinion in the משנה about a wrong thought during הולכה. ריש לקיש limits that opinion and says it does not apply to inner חטאות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's reason is that one could slaughter the animal right next to the מזבח and skip the walking, so it is not a necessary עבודה. Inner חטאות are slaughtered outside, but their blood must be sprinkled inside. So for them the carrying can never be avoided, and it counts as a real עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying the blood to the מזבח
Inner sin offerings, whose blood is sprinkled inside the היכל
Agrees (admits an exception to his usual view)
A service that cannot be skipped

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon deems it fit in the case of walking.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. 'Walking' means carrying the blood to the מזבח while having a wrong thought.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּהוֹלָכַת חַטָּאוֹת הַפְּנִימִיּוֹת
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon agrees about carrying the blood of the inner sin offerings
that a wrong thought disqualifies during it,
since it is a service that one cannot do away with.
phrases.notes: These animals are slaughtered outside, but the blood must go inside. So someone always has to carry it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַכְשִׁיר בְּהִילּוּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section on the משנה's ruling about הולכה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even according to רבי שמעון, a wrong thought while carrying the blood of inner חטאות disqualifies, because that carrying can never be skipped

steps.title: But inner offerings have no פיגול for רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש. רבי שמעון holds that any offering not brought on the outer מזבח like שלמים has no פיגול at all, so how can a thought disqualify inner חטאות?
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי שמעון said: any offering that is not on the outer מזבח like שלמים, one is not liable for it because of פיגול!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks ריש לקיש's statement using another known rule of רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that פיגול only applies to offerings brought on the outer מזבח, like שלמים. Inner חטאות are sprinkled inside, so they can never become פיגול. If so, how can a wrong thought during their carrying make any difference?

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? (introduces a contradiction)
The outer מזבח, in the courtyard
An offering ruined by a wrong thought about time; eating it brings כרת

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Shimon say:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ עַל מִזְבֵּחַ הַחִיצוֹן כִּשְׁלָמִים,
phrases.english: any offering that is not on the outer altar like peace offerings,
one is not liable for it because of פיגול!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's statement from Step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that רבי שמעון agrees a wrong thought disqualifies the carrying of inner חטאות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון holds there is no פיגול at all for offerings not on the outer מזבח, so a thought should have no effect on inner חטאות

steps.title: Not פיגול, but still disqualified, through a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא answers: רבי שמעון agrees the thought makes inner חטאות פסול, even though not פיגול. He learns it from a קל וחומר: if שלא לשמן, which is fine for שלמים, ruins a חטאת, then חוץ לזמנו, which ruins שלמים, should surely ruin a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: רבי שמעון would agree that it is disqualified, because of a קל וחומר. If 'not for its sake', which is valid with שלמים, makes a חטאת invalid, then 'outside its time', which makes שלמים invalid, should surely make חטאות invalid!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא answers the question. The wrong thought does not create פיגול with כרת, but it does make the offering פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from Step 7 only says there is no פיגול, meaning no כרת. It does not say the offering stays valid. The קל וחומר shows that a חטאת is stricter than שלמים, so a thought that ruins שלמים should surely ruin a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter case
Done for the sake of a different offering
Intending to eat or burn it after its allowed time
To disqualify (make the offering invalid, without כרת)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up פסול and פיגול. פיגול means eating it brings כרת. פסול just means the offering is invalid. Here inner חטאות become פסול, not פיגול.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, a wrong thought about time does not make inner חטאות פיגול, but it does make them פסול, learned by קל וחומר from שלמים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer separates two results of a wrong thought: invalidating the offering and bringing כרת. That lets ריש לקיש's statement and רבי שמעון's rule both stand.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Chanina, said:
He would agree that it is disqualified, because of a קל וחומר:
Just as 'not for its sake',
which was made valid with peace offerings,
is invalid with a sin offering;
'outside its time', which disqualifies peace offerings,
is it not logical that it should disqualify sin offerings?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מוֹדֶה הָיָה לִפְסוֹל מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separates פסול from פיגול and supports the פסול with a קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since inner חטאות have no פיגול for רבי שמעון, a wrong thought should have no effect on them at all
steps.terutzMaskana: The thought does not create פיגול with כרת, but it does make the inner חטאת פסול, learned by קל וחומר from שלמים

steps.title: Where do we learn that a wrong thought about place ruins an inner חטאת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא has a source for חוץ לזמנו but asks for a source for חוץ למקומו.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for 'outside its time.' From where do we learn 'outside its place'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question. It has proven that a wrong thought about time ruins an inner חטאת, and now it wants a source for a wrong thought about place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8's קל וחומר covered only חוץ לזמנו. But רבי שמעון's rule should also include a thought of eating the offering outside its proper area, חוץ למקומו. So the גמרא needs its own source for that.

keyTerms.meaning: Intending to eat or burn the offering after its allowed time
Intending to eat or burn the offering outside its allowed area
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: And we have found a source for 'outside its time,'
from where do we know 'outside its place'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַשְׁכְּחַן חוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ, חוּץ לִמְקוֹמוֹ מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the source from Step 8 and asks to extend it to a second kind of wrong thought.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that חוץ למקומו makes an inner חטאת פסול according to רבי שמעון.

steps.title: We cannot learn it from the thought about time
steps.stepSummary: Learning from חוץ לזמנו fails, because חוץ לזמנו is more severe: it can bring כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want to learn it from 'outside its time,' that is special, because it carries כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests one possible source and rejects it. You cannot copy the law from חוץ לזמנו to חוץ למקומו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thought of חוץ לזמנו can make an offering פיגול, and eating פיגול is punished with כרת. A thought of חוץ למקומו does not bring כרת. Since time is the more severe case, being strict there does not prove we should be strict about place.

keyTerms.meaning: Spiritual cutting off; the punishment for eating פיגול
What about X? It has a special strength. This is a standard way of rejecting a comparison

phrases.english: If you learn it from 'outside its time' —
what about 'outside its time'?
It is special, because it carries כרת!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִחוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ – מָה לְחוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ, שֶׁכֵּן כָּרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries the first possible source for the question in Step 9 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning חוץ למקומו from חוץ לזמנו.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: חוץ לזמנו has a severity that חוץ למקומו lacks: it brings כרת.

steps.title: We also cannot learn it from the thought about a different offering
steps.stepSummary: Learning from שלא לשמה also seems to fail, because שלא לשמה applies even on a private במה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want to learn it from 'not for its sake,' that is special, because it applies even on a private altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second source, שלא לשמה, and pushes it away too. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wrong thought of שלא לשמה counts even on a private במה. A wrong thought about place does not, because a במה has no set area for eating. Since שלא לשמה reaches further, we cannot assume חוץ למקומו is just as strong.

keyTerms.meaning: Doing the service while thinking of a different kind of offering
A private altar, allowed during certain periods before the בית המקדש
Applies; is in effect

phrases.english: If you learn it from 'not for its sake' —
that is special, because it applies on a private altar!
phrases.notes: A private altar has no special area for eating, so a wrong thought about place is meaningless there.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִשֶּׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ – שֶׁכֵּן נוֹהֵג בְּבָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries the second possible source after the first one was rejected, and pushes this one away too.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning חוץ למקומו from שלא לשמה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שלא לשמה seems to apply even on a private במה, where חוץ למקומו has no meaning.

steps.title: The objection fails: פסח and חטאת were never brought on a private altar
steps.stepSummary: שלא לשמה only ruins פסח and חטאת, and these never went on a במה. So in practice it does not apply on a במה, and we can learn from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which offerings does 'not for its sake' ruin? Only a פסח and a חטאת. And a פסח and a חטאת were never brought on a private altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the objection from Step 11. Once that falls, we can learn חוץ למקומו from שלא לשמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thought of שלא לשמה only makes פסח and חטאת פסול. Neither of these was ever brought on a private במה. So the claim that 'it applies on a במה' has no real meaning, and nothing stops the קל וחומר from working for חוץ למקומו.

keyTerms.meaning: The קרבן פסח
Were not offered
In what case?

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, both a wrong thought about time and a wrong thought about place make an inner חטאת פסול, though not פיגול. Both are learned by a קל וחומר from שלא לשמה. The objection that 'שלא לשמה applies on a במה' fails, because פסח and חטאת were never brought on a במה.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say that שלא לשמה is unimportant. It says that the 'במה' difference is not real: the offerings that שלא לשמה ruins never went on a במה at all.

phrases.english: In which offerings does 'not for its sake' apply? —
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some leave it out.

phrases.english: in a פסח and a חטאת;
and a פסח and a חטאת were not offered on a private altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָן בְּמַאי נוֹהֵג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 11, so שלא לשמה works as the source asked for in Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the objection is empty: the claimed strength never actually applies.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שלא לשמה seemed stronger because it applies on a private במה, so we could not learn חוץ למקומו from it.
steps.terutzMaskana: שלא לשמה only ruins פסח and חטאת, which never went on a במה. So the learning stands: חוץ למקומו also makes an inner חטאת פסול.

steps.title: A second source: a הקש linking time and place
steps.stepSummary: Instead of a קל וחומר, the גמרא learns חוץ למקומו from a הקש. The same פסוק mentions both 'third day' (חוץ לזמנו) and 'פיגול' (חוץ למקומו), so they share the same law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, say it comes from a הקש: 'third' refers to חוץ לזמנו, and 'פיגול' refers to חוץ למקומו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another answer to the question from step 9: what is the source for חוץ למקומו? It says the פסוק itself puts time and place side by side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 10-12 had to defend a קל וחומר against objections. A הקש does not need the two cases to be equally severe. Since the פסוק links them, whatever is true of חוץ לזמנו is also true of חוץ למקומו, so the 'כרת' objection from step 10 no longer matters.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you wish, say', which introduces another answer
Linking two laws because the פסוק places them together
'Third' day, read as the thought of eating after the proper time
A ruined offering, read here as the thought of eating outside the proper place

steps.whatToRemember: Two sources for חוץ למקומו: a קל וחומר from שלא לשמה (steps 11-12), or a הקש from ויקרא 7:18.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
it is a juxtaposition;
phrases.notes: He means we don't need the קל וחומר at all. The פסוק links the two cases directly.

phrases.english: "third" – this is beyond its time,
"piggul" – this is outside its place.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: הֶקֵּישָׁא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the question of step 9, side-stepping the objections of steps 10-12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative source (הקש instead of קל וחומר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We needed a קל וחומר, and it was open to objections.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק links חוץ לזמנו and חוץ למקומו, so they share the same law.

steps.title: If רבי שמעון follows his son, carrying counts only from the אולם inward
steps.stepSummary: If רבי שמעון agrees with his son that the area between the אולם and the מזבח counts as צפון, an inner חטאת could be slaughtered right by the אולם. So a wrong thought while carrying its blood counts only from the doorway of the אולם inward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If you say רבי שמעון agrees with his son, who said the area between the אולם and the מזבח is considered צפון, then a thought does not count while carrying the blood of inner חטאות except from the doorway of the אולם and inward.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new topic: exactly where along the path of carrying a wrong thought ruins the offering, according to רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule assumed here is that only needed carrying counts. If the animal could have been slaughtered right at the doorway of the אולם, then carrying the blood up to that point was not needed. Only the carrying from there into the היכל really counts.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you come to say', which sets up 'if this, then that'
Carrying the blood toward where it is placed
The front hall of the בית המקדש building, before the היכל
The northern area where קדשי קדשים like a חטאת are slaughtered
חטאות whose blood is brought inside, to the היכל or קודש הקדשים

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the carrying before the אולם is unimportant in general. He means a wrong thought during that stretch does not ruin the offering, because that stretch was not needed.

phrases.english: Rava said:
If you come to say
Rabbi Shimon holds like his son,
phrases.notes: His son is רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

phrases.english: who said: between the Entrance Hall and the altar is "north";
intent is not effective
in carrying the inner sin offerings,
except from the doorway of the Entrance Hall and inward.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אִם תִּימְצֵי לוֹמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר לַהּ כִּבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to ריש לקיש's statement in Step 6 and narrows it. If the area by the אולם counts as צפון, only the carrying from the אולם doorway inward is truly unavoidable, so only there does a thought disqualify.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the area by the אולם is צפון, a thought during carrying the blood of inner חטאות counts only from the אולם doorway inward.

steps.title: If רבי שמעון follows רבי יהודה, carrying the בזיכין counts only outside the היכל
steps.stepSummary: If the floor of the עזרה can make things holy like the מזבח, the לבונה could be burned as soon as it leaves the building. Inside the היכל, the שולחן could stand anywhere. So only the carrying from the היכל doorway outward is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say he holds like רבי יהודה, who said the inside of the עזרה makes things holy, then a thought does not count while carrying the removed בזיכין except from the doorway of the היכל and outward.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second version of his rule. This one is about carrying the bowls of לבונה out of the היכל, if רבי שמעון holds like רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the שולחן could be placed anywhere in the היכל, walking inside the היכל was not needed. Since the whole עזרה could serve like the מזבח, carrying past the building's exit was not needed either. That leaves only the stretch from the היכל doorway outward, through the אולם.

keyTerms.meaning: The courtyard of the בית המקדש
Makes holy, here meaning it works like the מזבח
Removing the bowls of לבונה from the שולחן to burn them
The main inner hall where the שולחן and מנורה stood

phrases.english: And if you come to say
he holds like Rabbi Yehuda,
who said: the inside of the courtyard sanctifies;
phrases.notes: He means the courtyard floor itself can act like the מזבח, so things could be burned right there.

phrases.english: intent is not effective
in carrying the removed bowls,
except from the doorway of the Sanctuary and outward.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second application of רבא's 'only needed carrying counts' idea, now for the בזיכין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the עזרה makes things holy, a thought during carrying the בזיכין counts only from the היכל doorway outward.

steps.title: If היכל and אולם are equally holy, only the אולם doorway counts
steps.stepSummary: If the היכל and אולם share one level of holiness, the שולחן could stand in the אולם too. Then the only needed carrying is right at the אולם doorway.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say he holds that the holiness of the היכל and the אולם is one, then a thought counts only from the doorway of the אולם and outward.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a third, narrower version of the בזיכין rule. This time he adds the idea that the היכל and the אולם have the same holiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the שולחן could stand in the אולם, then carrying through the אולם is also unnecessary. The needed stretch shrinks to the doorway of the אולם itself, the last step before the עזרה.

keyTerms.meaning: The holiness level of the היכל and of the אולם
'It is one', meaning they are the same

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, a wrong thought during carrying counts only on the stretch that was truly needed. Where that stretch is depends on which other opinions he holds.

phrases.english: And if you come to say, he holds:
the holiness of the Sanctuary and the Entrance Hall is one;
intent is not effective
except from the doorway of the Entrance Hall and outward.
phrases.notes: He means right at the אולם's doorway, since the שולחן could have been in the אולם and the courtyard could serve as the מזבח.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר, סָבַר: קְדוּשַּׁת הֵיכָל וְאוּלָם – חֲדָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows step 15 further by adding that the היכל and אולם are equally holy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the היכל and אולם are equally holy, a thought counts only at the אולם doorway going outward.

steps.title: If the doorway counts as inside, only a hand-stretch is left
steps.stepSummary: If רבי שמעון also holds that the inside of the doorway counts as inside, the שולחן could stand in the doorway itself. Then a wrong thought could not matter even for one step, only for the moment the hand stretches out.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that the inside of the doorway counts like inside, then a thought does not work even for one step. It works only for the time it takes him to stretch out his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא shrinks the carrying of the frankincense one more level. If the doorway itself counts as inside, there is no walking left at all, only a hand reaching out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 16 the only carrying left was right at the doorway of the אולם. Now, if the doorway space itself counts as inside, the שולחן could stand right in the doorway. So a wrong thought can only matter during the short moment the כהן reaches his hand out of the doorway.

keyTerms.meaning: The space inside the doorway itself
Counts like the inside area
A step (walking)
Stretching out his hand

phrases.english: And if you say
that the inside of the doorway is like inside,
then a thought does not work
even for one step,
but only for the time it takes to stretch out his hand.
phrases.notes: He means the moment the כהן reaches out of the doorway to put the frankincense down outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר תּוֹךְ הַפֶּתַח כְּלִפְנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds one more assumption to step 16 and shrinks the carrying even further.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the doorway counts as inside, a wrong thought during carrying the frankincense matters only during the hand-stretch out of the doorway.

steps.title: If carrying without walking is not carrying, no thought matters at all
steps.stepSummary: If רבי שמעון also holds that moving something without walking is not called carrying, then even the hand-stretch does not count, and a wrong thought has no effect at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say he holds that carrying not done by foot is not called carrying, then a thought does not work at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא takes the last step of the shrinking. If only walking counts as carrying, the hand-stretch is not carrying, so nothing is left for a wrong thought to ruin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 17 only the reach of the hand was left. If a hand movement without walking is not called הולכה at all, then even that is gone. So in רבי שמעון's view, under all these assumptions, a thought during carrying the frankincense does nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying the offering (or its blood) toward the place of service
Not by foot, without walking
At all

steps.whatToRemember: Step by step (steps 14-18), רבא showed that in רבי שמעון's view the carrying can shrink to a hand-stretch, or to nothing at all, so a wrong thought during it may have no effect.

phrases.english: And if you say he holds:
carrying that is not by foot
is not called carrying,
then a thought does not work at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר, סָבַר: הוֹלָכָה שֶׁלֹּא בָּרֶגֶל לֹא שְׁמָהּ הוֹלָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes away even the hand-stretch left in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If carrying without walking is not carrying, a wrong thought while carrying the frankincense has no effect at all.

steps.title: אביי asks whether a non-כהן may carry the blood
steps.stepSummary: אביי sends a question to רב חסדא through his speaker: what is the law if a זר carries the blood?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב חסדא's speaker: Ask רב חסדא for me: if a non-כהן carries the blood, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts here. אביי asks whether הולכה done by a זר ruins the offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most services with the blood must be done by a כהן, and a זר doing them makes the offering פסול. אביי wants to know if carrying the blood is one of those services, or if a זר may do it.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: the speaker who repeated the רב's lesson out loud to the crowd
Ask him
A non-כהן
What is the law?

phrases.english: Abaye said
to Rav Chisda's speaker,
phrases.notes: This is the man who stood by the teacher and called out his words loudly so everyone could hear.

phrases.english: Ask Rav Chisda:
carrying done by a non-kohen, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְאָמוֹרֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא, בְּעִי מִינֵּיהּ מֵרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about הולכה, now about who may do it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether carrying the blood by a זר makes the offering פסול.

steps.title: רב חסדא: valid, and a פסוק supports it
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that carrying by a זר is valid, and brings support from a פסוק describing the קרבן פסח in the days of יאשיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is valid, and a verse supports me: 'And they slaughtered the פסח, and the כהנים threw the blood from their hand, and the לוים skinned.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers אביי's question: a זר may carry the blood. He shows a פסוק to back this up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names the כהנים only at the throwing of the blood, and says they took the blood 'from their hand', from others who handed it to them. So the steps before throwing, like carrying, did not need a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Valid, the offering is fine
A verse supports me
Throwing the blood on the מזבח
From their hand, handed over by others

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא: הולכה by a זר is כשרה. The כהן is needed from the throwing of the blood and on.

phrases.english: He said to him: it is valid,
and a verse supports me:
"And they slaughtered the Pesach,
and the kohanim threw the blood from their hand,
phrases.notes: 'From their hand' means others handed the blood over; the כהנים only start at the throwing.

phrases.english: and the Levites skinned."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כְּשֵׁרָה, וּמִקְרָא מְסַיְּיעֵנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question from step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הולכה by a זר is valid, supported by the פסוק that names כהנים only from the throwing of the blood.
steps.raayaObject: That a זר may carry the blood

steps.title: רב ששת begins an objection from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת starts to quote a ברייתא that opens with 'a זר, and an אונן,' to challenge רב חסדא's ruling that a זר may carry the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת raises an objection from a ברייתא: 'A non-כהן, or a mourner on the day of a close relative's death...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. רב ששת begins quoting a ברייתא, and the rest of it comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא just said a זר may carry the blood. רב ששת opens a ברייתא that lists a זר alongside an אונן, people who normally may not do עבודה. Putting a זר in that list hints that a זר's carrying may be a problem, which would clash with רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-כהן, someone not allowed to do the עבודה
A mourner on the day a close relative died, before the burial

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop here thinking the challenge is finished. These words are only the start of the ברייתא. Its ruling, the part that actually challenges רב חסדא, comes next.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet raises an objection:
A non-priest, or an acute mourner,

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge to רב חסדא's answer in Step 20 that carrying by a זר is valid.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that a זר's carrying of the blood is valid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא groups a זר with other disqualified people such as an אונן. This suggests a זר's service, carrying included, may be invalid. The full ruling appears in the continuing text.
